assumptions: PS1, PS2, PS3 and S1, S2, S3 are modeled as integer input flags used in guards because the NL calls them inputs and combines arrival sensors with motion states.
hbrg values are abstracted as 1 for upward drive, -1 for downward drive, and 0 for stop because the NL specifies three distinguishable output conditions but not numeric encodings.
When multiple request guards are simultaneously true from the same floor, transition priority follows the order stated in the NL and emitted in the DSL.

M1_guard_off_by_one.description: guard `>= N` mistakenly written as `>= N-1` (fires one cycle too early)

M2_wrong_transition_target.description: transition `A -> B` written as `A -> C` (wrong target state)

M3_unreachable_target.description: guard threshold set far too high (`>= 99999`), target state never reached

M4_missing_forced_transition.description: forced transition `! ...` line missing (global event ignored)

M6_wrong_effect_value.description: effect assigns wrong constant (`var = N` → `var = N+100`)

scenario_results.description: default-init dispatches to floor 1 stop condition, no floor request stays stopped at F1, then Reset from a floor still forces F1.
scenario_results.name: default_init_no_request_and_reset_from_floor

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start at F1 with a PS2 request should move upward to MU2, and Reset from that motion state should force F1.
scenario_results.name: f1_ps2_to_mu2_then_reset_from_motion

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start at F1 with a PS3 request should select the upward branch to MU3 with upward drive output.
scenario_results.name: f1_ps3_to_mu3_up_drive

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start in MU2 with S2 arrival should stop at F2, then immediately check PS3 and continue upward to MU3.
scenario_results.name: mu2_arrival_f2_immediate_ps3_to_mu3

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start in MU3 with S3 arrival should stop at F3, then immediately check PS1 and continue downward to MD1.
scenario_results.name: mu3_arrival_f3_immediate_ps1_to_md1

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start in MD1 with S1 arrival should stop at F1, then immediately check PS2 and continue upward to MU2.
scenario_results.name: md1_arrival_f1_immediate_ps2_to_mu2

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start in MD2 with S2 arrival should stop at F2, then immediately check PS1 and continue downward to MD1.
scenario_results.name: md2_arrival_f2_immediate_ps1_to_md1

scenario_results.description: explicit-hot-start at F3 with a PS2 request should move downward to MD2, and Reset from down motion should force F1.
scenario_results.name: f3_ps2_to_md2_then_reset_from_down_motion

evidence: DSL defines F1, F2, F3, MU2, MU3, MD1, MD2.
DSL includes F1->MU2[PS2 > 0], F1->MU3[PS3 > 0], F2->MU3[PS3 > 0], F2->MD1[PS1 > 0], F3->MD1[PS1 > 0], F3->MD2[PS2 > 0].
DSL includes MU2->F2[S2 > 0], MU3->F3[S3 > 0], MD1->F1[S1 > 0], MD2->F2[S2 > 0].
enter actions set hbrg=1 for MU2/MU3, hbrg=-1 for MD1/MD2, hbrg=0 for F1/F2/F3.
DSL includes [*] -> F1 and ! * -> F1 :: Reset.
findings.summary: The DSL closely matches the NL elevator FSM: required floor states, motion states, request-triggered departures, sensor-triggered arrivals, stop/up/down hbrg outputs, initial F1 state, and forced Reset-to-F1 behavior are represented.

evidence: GroundingMap marks all seven leaf states as required and present.
GroundingMap marks all listed request and arrival transitions as required and present.
inspect_model_to_json_summary reports n_states_leaf=7, n_transitions_normal=11, n_transitions_forced=7, n_variables=7, n_events=1.
sim_summary reports ok=true with 8/8 scenarios passed.
findings.summary: Core component coverage is strong for states, transitions, guards, actions, inputs, output, initialization, and reset. Estimated NFRR tier: T3 strong reviewed candidate.

evidence: GroundingMap source_summary assumes transition priority follows the order stated in the NL when multiple request guards are simultaneously true.
The NL lists individual triggers but does not define behavior when PS1/PS2/PS3 or sensors are simultaneously asserted.
sim_summary covers 8 passing scenarios but examples focus on single active request/sensor paths.
findings.summary: Scenario evidence is good but not exhaustive for all ambiguous concurrent-request or persistent-sensor combinations; this is an oracle coverage limitation rather than a clear model defect because the NL does not specify tie-breaking semantics beyond the listed transitions.

evidence: DSL declares PS1, PS2, PS3, S1, S2, S3, hbrg uniformly as def int.
design_diagnostics_summary lists W_UNWRITTEN_READ_VAR for PS1/PS2/PS3/S1/S2/S3.
design_diagnostics_summary identifies nl_external_input_vars as PS1, PS2, PS3, S1, S2, S3.
design_diagnostics_summary lists W_UNREFERENCED_VAR for hbrg, which is expected for a pure output that does not affect guards.
findings.summary: The DSL uses plain integer variables for external inputs and the hbrg output, relying on grounding/diagnostic metadata to distinguish input versus output roles. This creates advisory diagnostics but is consistent with the NL and not a blocking issue.

evidence: NL: hbrg output distinguishes upward drive, downward drive, and stop conditions.
GroundingMap source_summary states hbrg values are abstracted as 1 for upward, -1 for downward, and 0 for stop because numeric encodings are unspecified.
findings.summary: The numeric encoding of hbrg as 1/up, -1/down, and 0/stop is an abstraction, but it is justified because the NL requires distinguishable output conditions without specifying concrete numeric values.

evidence: review_policy.model_review is blocking_major_only.

findings.summary: Evaluation risk is limited to oracle incompleteness around unspecified simultaneous inputs and exact run-to-completion interpretation of 'immediately checks'; no evidence suggests a major mismatch under the supplied policy.
